items.title: The Problem of Pattern and Scale in Ecology: The Robert H. MacArthur Award Lecture
items.summary: It is argued that the problem of pattern and scale is the central problem in ecology, unifying population biology and ecosystems science, and marrying basic and applied ecology. Applied challenges, such as the prediction of the ecological causes and consequences of global climate change, require the interfacing of phenomena that occur on very different scales of space, time, and ecological organization. items.title: Perceptual symbol systems
items.summary: Prior to the twentieth century, theories of knowledge were inherently perceptual. Since then, developments in logic, statistics, and programming languages have inspired amodal theories that rest on principles fundamentally different from those underlying perception. In addition, perceptual approaches have become widely viewed as untenable because they are assumed to implement recording systems, not conceptual systems. items.title: An Introduction to Continuity Science:Bringing Existing Fields Together to Explore Personal Information and Conscious Continuity
items.summary: Could surviving physical information support the reconstruction of a temporally specific person, and would such a reconstruction preserve the original person’s conscious experience? This personal, non-peer-reviewed introductory paper proposes Continuity Science as a working name for bringing existing fields together to investigate what persists, changes, or is lost in a person over time, including the stronger question of whether conscious experience could continue through substantial physical change. items.title: Admissibility of "Raw Neural Data" as Criminal Evidence in Criminal Courts: A Jurisprudential, Legal, and Neuroscientific Analysis
items.summary: The growing convergence of neuroscience and criminal law, known as neurolaw, has presented a new challenge regarding the admissibility of "raw neural data" (e.g., EEG signals and brain activity) as criminal evidence in judicial proceedings. This study aims to examine the position of these data within Iran’s criminal evidence system, employing a descriptive-analytical method with an interdisciplinary approach to assess the threefold dimensions of scientific, legal, and jurisprudential aspects of the issue. items.title: THE CONCEPT OF DHARNIYA VEGA AND ITS IMPORTANCE TO MAINTANACE OF HEALTHY AND HAPPY LIFE
items.summary: Dharniya Vega, described in Ayurveda, refers to the voluntary suppression of harmful mental, verbal, and physical urges to maintain health and ethical conduct. Classical Ayurveda texts, particularly the Charak Samhita Sutra sthan chapter 7, Vega and types of Dharniya Vega, emphasize that controlling negative emotions such as anger (Krodha), greed (Lobha), jealousy (Irshya), excessive attachment (Raha), harsh speech and unethical, psychological, and moral health failure to regulate these impulses may contribute to psychosomatic disorders, emotional instability, and impaired social functioning.

items.title: Cortex-wide neuronal dynamics underpin quasi-periodic patterns in resting-state fMRI
items.summary: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) captures whole-brain activity fluctuations non-invasively in humans and animals. Beyond task/stimuli-locked responses, fMRI measures large-scale patterned activity during rest. Among these, quasi-periodic patterns (QPPs) represent recurring waves of activity that unfold over seconds and exhibit consistent spatiotemporal characteristics. items.summary: Anger-related irritability is a leading reason for referral to child and adolescent mental health services. items.title: Exercise therapy for chronic pain: an updated perspective on mesocorticolimbic system function
items.summary: Patients with chronic pain often experience behavioral issues linked to pain, depression, and other emotional disorders. These problems stem from dysfunction in the mesocorticolimbic system, and exercise offers a safe, accessible, and effective alternative. It not only reduces pain but also activates multiple neural pathways, helping restore normal function. items.title: Brain sites involved in endogenous analgesia
items.summary: Pain modulation is a fundamental survival mechanism that prioritises, shapes, and suppresses nociceptive inputs to optimise behaviour. Although acute pain signals potential or actual tissue damage, sustained pain can impair essential behaviours, necessitating modulatory circuits that dynamically regulate nociception according to context and motivational state. items.title: Computation or Weight Adaptation? Rethinking the Role of Plasticity in Learning
items.summary: The human brain is an adaptive learning system that can generalize to new tasks and unfamiliar environments. The traditional view is that such adaptive behavior requires a structural change of the learning system (e.g., via neural plasticity). In this work, we use artificial neural networks, specifically large language models (LLMs), to challenge this traditional view and suggest that such adaptive behavior can be also achieved solely through computation if the learning system is sufficiently trained. items.summary: Abstract Early life adversity has a lasting impact on the endocannabinoid (eCB) system based on animal models. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

OBJECTIVES: This meta-analytic review was conducted to determine the extent to which social relationships influence risk for mortality, which aspects of social relationships are most highly predictive, and which factors may moderate the risk. items.title: Spontaneous neuropathic pain
items.summary: Spontaneous pain is a highly prevalent and disabling consequence of neuropathic disorders, yet it remains mechanistically underdefined and therapeutically underserved. Historically, preclinical animal models and clinical trials have been overwhelmingly biased toward stimulus-evoked hypersensitivity, relegating spontaneous pain to a secondary manifestation. items.summary: Most commercial UAV platforms still lack a mandatory pre-flight identity check, leaving ground control stations exposed to impersonation and unauthorized takeover. This paper proposes a facial recognition-based pilot authentication system using a custom four-block Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to classify three identity classes: Pilot 1, Pilot 2, and Stranger.
